stem: Which of the following is the formula for Standard Form, Foci & Eccentricity?
candidateDistractors: \(Ax^2 + Cy^2 + Dx + Ey + F = 0 \ \xrightarrow{\text{complete squares}}\ \text{standard form}\)
trapHints: Hyperbola uses PLUS: c² = a² + b²: The ellipse has \(c^2 = a^2 - b^2\); the hyperbola has \(c^2 = a^2 + b^2\). Carrying the ellipse's minus sign into a hyperbola is the single most common slip in this subtopic.

A hyperbola's eccentricity is always greater than 1: Since \(c^2 = a^2 + b^2 > a^2\), we have \(c > a\) and so \(e = \dfrac{c}{a} > 1\) for every hyperbola. An eccentricity computed as \(<1\) means you used the ellipse relation \(c^2 = a^2 - b^2\) by mistake.
